back: Used to suggest, persuade, or criticize (e.g., 'Why don't we go out?') [12].
Use 'not' after the subject (e.g., 'Did she not realise...?') [12].
Can use never, no, nobody, nothing instead of -n't (e.g., 'Why do you never help?') [12].
Use 'Why didn't...?' (e.g., 'Why didn't you tell me?') [12].
Negative questions with falling intonation (e.g., 'Haven't you grown!') [12].
Used to check understanding or express surprise (e.g., 'Tala's lost her what?') [12].
Stressed wh-word focuses on part of the sentence (e.g., 'Leon's arriving when?') [12].
Wh-questions can refer to a following that-clause (e.g., 'When do you reckon (that) you'll finish?') [12].

front: Have you ... you might be wrong?

back: He's sold what? / He's done what? [13].

front: Who do you ... will read your blog?
What did you say ... in these biscuits?
back: that is (NOT What did you say is in these biscuits) [12, 13].
